stories.body: President Donald Trump issued an executive order pausing parts of a new bipartisan Russia sanctions law just before it was due to take effect. The law targets Russian officials, banks and oil-shipping networks, and authorizes tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. Trump said the pause was in the national interest, days after announcing a US deal to buy Russian diesel. Lawmakers from both parties criticized the move, saying full implementation could pressure Moscow to engage seriously in peace talks with Ukraine.
stories.headline: Trump suspends new Russia sanctions after signing them into law

stories.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked European allies for an additional €70 billion to fund Ukraine's war effort next year, including air-defense support for the winter. The request comes as relations with President Trump have deteriorated following the US decision to ease Russia sanctions alongside a diesel-supply deal with Moscow.
stories.headline: Zelensky seeks €70 billion in European military funding as ties with Trump worsen

stories.body: Brazil's space research agency says Amazon deforestation fell 41.8% in the year through July, to 3,335 square kilometres, the lowest annual total since records began in 1988. Deforestation in the Cerrado savanna also fell by about 24%. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva credited stronger enforcement and renewed his goal of ending illegal deforestation by 2030, while the figures give him a boost before an October 25 runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, who has promised a different approach to the Amazon.
stories.headline: Brazil reports Amazon deforestation at its lowest recorded level before election runoff

stories.body: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in several West Bank villages, burning cars and trees and injuring at least 20 people, according to Palestinian authorities. In Abu Falah, witnesses said about 80 settlers used clubs, stones and slingshots against farmers; Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was beaten, and her passport, phone, wallet and equipment were stolen. The attacks came amid a sharp rise in settler violence during the annual olive harvest.
stories.headline: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters and injure US photojournalist in West Bank

stories.body: France is preparing for more than 1,000 demonstrations over living costs, fuel prices and the government's handling of the economy. The protests began with student blockades and have drawn support from farmers, health workers, public-sector workers and figures associated with the 2018 Yellow Vest movement. Authorities have warned of a potentially violent Saturday and have convened a crisis response, while parties are seeking to turn the unrest into momentum before the presidential election.
stories.headline: France braces for nationwide protests as Yellow Vests join student movement

stories.body: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced an interim administration for Tigray, with elections planned within six months. The northern region has again clashed with federal forces since September, reviving conflict after the 2020–22 war that killed hundreds of thousands of people.
stories.headline: Ethiopia appoints interim administration in Tigray and plans elections within six months

stories.body: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving the role less than a week after President Trump appointed her. Her first briefing lasted about 14 minutes and drew criticism over her preparedness, while scrutiny focused on Trump's description of her as an attorney despite her not having passed a bar exam. Trump said he had advised her to reconsider the job because of the treatment she received from the press.
stories.headline: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia leaves after five days

stories.body: Representative Haley Stevens endorsed Abdul El-Sayed after losing Michigan's Democratic Senate primary but has made little public effort to campaign or fundraise for him. Some of her former supporters, particularly among Black and Jewish voters, remain resistant to El-Sayed, while his Republican opponent Mike Rogers is seeking to exploit those divisions. El-Sayed has campaigned to repair relationships with those communities and has raised far more than Rogers in recent months.
stories.headline: Haley Stevens remains largely absent from Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate campaign

stories.body: Former Indiana governor Mitch Daniels said Vice President JD Vance and other Republicans are wrong to move away from the party's traditional support for free markets. Daniels said market dynamism can disrupt culture and tradition but remains essential to preserving the American dream. He argued that the Republican Party's populist and protectionist turn, including support for broad tariffs, could create space for a new pro-freedom political movement.
stories.headline: Mitch Daniels criticizes JD Vance's retreat from free-market economics

stories.body: Podemos and the Front Ampli alliance failed to agree on a unified nationwide slate before the deadline for the November 29 general election. They will run separately in major constituencies including Madrid, though local agreements remain in places such as Valencia, the Canary Islands and parts of Aragón and the Balearic Islands. In Catalonia, Podemos has an arrangement with ERC, while the Comuns will run with the Front Ampli; the PSOE and several left-wing parties did agree on a joint Senate list.
stories.headline: Spain's alternative left fails to reach a nationwide election pact

stories.body: PSOE spokeswoman and Lleida MP Montse Mínguez resigned from all party and parliamentary positions after reports that her partner's property company manages dozens of rental homes and has carried out evictions. Mínguez said the activity was legal but that stepping aside was best for the party's collective project. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he had urged her not to resign and blamed the personal toll of increasingly harsh political attacks.
stories.headline: PSOE spokeswoman Montse Mínguez resigns over reports about her partner's property businesses

stories.body: Spain and Italy agreed to coordinate the end of border controls at ports and airports that Rome imposed on travelers from Spain and Madrid then mirrored. The controls followed the Ceuta migration crisis and had become a point of conflict between Pedro Sánchez and Giorgia Meloni. At the EU summit, member states also issued a declaration of support recognizing Ceuta and Melilla as Europe's borders in Africa.
stories.headline: Spain and Italy agree to end Schengen controls imposed after Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Spain's ombudsman, Ángel Gabilondo, has asked the Constitutional Court to suspend the Supreme Court's decision preventing many people naturalized under the Democratic Memory Law from voting in the November 29 election. The ruling affects about 163,000 citizens unless consulates can establish that they descend from exiles. The Supreme Court said the integrity of the overseas electoral register must prevail, while Gabilondo argues that Spanish nationality necessarily carries voting rights.
stories.headline: Ombudsman challenges suspension of voting rights for citizens naturalized under Democratic Memory Law

stories.body: The Semaf train drivers' union has called a 24-hour strike across the Renfe group on October 29 after talks with the Transport Ministry, Adif, Renfe and the rail-safety agency failed. The union says agreements on weather-emergency protocols, staffing, responses to track incidents and rolling-stock reliability remain blocked. Renfe says it has fulfilled the commitments assigned to it and warns the strike could affect thousands of travelers.
stories.headline: Train drivers call 24-hour Renfe strike for 29 October over railway safety

stories.body: A Sabadell judge has ordered Santi Laiglesia to stand trial for the 2001 murder of librarian Helena Jubany, 25 years after her death. The case against another suspect was provisionally closed, while the judge rejected Laiglesia's request for further investigation. Prosecutors and Jubany's family seek 26 years in prison, alleging that she was drugged, held unlawfully and thrown down a building's lightwell; the trial is not expected before summer 2027.
stories.headline: Judge sends Helena Jubany murder case to trial 25 years after her death

stories.body: The Generalitat has bought the RACC headquarters on Avinguda Diagonal for €75.5 million as part of the future Clínic-UB health campus. RACC can remain in the 36,699-square-metre building until 2030, while the government pays in four interest-free annual installments. The broader project includes a new Hospital Clínic, University of Barcelona medical and health-science facilities, research centers and housing, with construction planned to begin in 2030.
stories.headline: Catalan government buys RACC headquarters for Clínic-UB medical campus project

stories.body: Barcelona's public health agency is releasing 80,000 male tiger mosquitoes each week from June through mid-November in a pilot project at Parc de la Ciutadella, the zoo and Plaça de les Corts. The males carry Wolbachia bacteria, which makes eggs produced with wild females nonviable and is intended to cut mosquito numbers by half in the trial areas. Officials say the male mosquitoes do not bite and the bacteria are safe for people, animals and the environment.
stories.headline: Barcelona releases 80,000 sterile tiger mosquitoes each week to curb the pest
